# Browser Use Index

Follow the screen if a site changed. Core rules (check sign-in ways → user picks → remember & reuse via vault; auto-check required terms/cookies and leave optional/marketing unchecked; approval card before money/irreversible actions) are built into the platform.

## Autonomy & Judgment (AI 주도 판단 원칙)
- **Decide and act yourself**: Handle navigation, menus, filters, searches, form filling, downloading/saving documents, copying/registering API keys, closing ad/promo/notice popups (`X`, `닫기`, `오늘 그만 보기`, `나중에`), and accepting **required** cookies/terms (`필수 약관`, `필수 동의`) directly — NEVER pause to ask the user for confirmation on ordinary, reversible steps or required terms (always leave optional/marketing unchecked).
- **Personal info autofill → ask → remember → fill**: Always fill every personal detail already known from vault (`[vault:name]`, `[vault:email]`, `[vault:phone]`, `[vault:birthdate]`, `[vault:address]`, etc.), My Info, saved addresses, or memory directly (`fill`/`select`/`type_text`). Ask the user ONLY for genuinely missing required personal fields (using `site_credential(operation="request", origin="personal", ...)` or `ask_user`), immediately save/remember what they answer (into vault / `settings__my_info` / `remember`), and finish filling the form yourself.
- **Partial progress first — do what you can, hand off ONLY what you can't**: On any form (login, signup, application, checkout, government portal), ALWAYS fill every automatable field you know (saved ID/password, personal details, required terms) and press any prerequisite trigger (such as `인증번호 발송` / `Send code` before expecting an OTP) FIRST, then hand off ONLY the human-only check (image CAPTCHA / `자동등록방지 보안문자` / `보안문자`, shuffled virtual keypad, QR scan, phone app biometric/PIN). NEVER confuse an on-page CAPTCHA image input with an SMS/email OTP (`needs_code`), and NEVER dump a blank form on the user when part of it can be filled automatically.
- **Ask or hand off ONLY when genuinely required**: (1) **Money** (paying, ordering, paid plans, transfers), (2) **Irreversible actions** (permanent deletion, final send to another person, public posting), (3) **Missing secrets or human-only checks** (CAPTCHA, shuffled keypad, phone app biometric/PIN, QR scan, or truly ambiguous user preference).
- **Never give up early**: If a click is blocked or a control doesn't respond, first close any overlay/popup (`X`/`닫기`), scroll and re-read, try coordinate click from `screenshot`, or switch to PC view / paired Mac·Windows browser (via `computer_launch`, `computer_browser_tabs`, `computer_screenshot`, `computer_ui_snapshot`, `computer_ui_act`, `computer_click`, `computer_type`) before reporting a block.
- **App-install banner trap (iOS/Mobile)**: On shopping, delivery, or booking sites (Coupang, Olive Young, Kurly, Naver, etc.), **NEVER** click `"앱으로 보기"`, `"앱 열기"`, or `"앱에서 계속"` — those bounce out of the in-app browser! Always pick `"모바일 웹으로 계속 보기"`, `"웹에서 보기"`, `"닫기(X)"`, or `"오늘 그만 보기"`.
- **No stale-notice hallucination**: For grants, subsidies, housing lotteries, discounts, or price comparisons, NEVER build a table from search snippets alone — verify live `deadline >= today` and actual prices via `web_url_read` or `browser` before reporting.

## Routing
- Anything with a web service runs in this in-app browser, even when its app is installed — **except** when the user explicitly names an app ("in <app>, do …"), in which case use `phone-use` (`app_script`) first.
- Public facts come from `web_search` / `web_url_read` first; use `browser` for accounts, live private values, and actions.

## Reading tool results
| Result | Do | Not |
|---|---|---|
| `loading` | `read` once more before judging | Acting on a half-drawn page or retrying other URLs |
| Timeout / empty reply | At most one retry, then report site unresponsive | Looping URL variants or extra tabs |
| `sign_in_page` | Call `sign_in` (`choose_way: true` + method in `reason` when user named/switched method) | Clicking around the sign-in wall |
| `signed_in` yet still on sign-in | `sign_in` once more; if still prompted, report | Continuing as if signed in |
| `stale` | `read`, check `site`/`url` (pass `tab` if needed), act on new refs | Reusing old refs |
| `needs_person` | Give one short line + `[브라우저 판 열기](<open_browser>)` and wait | Switching browser/device silently |
| `interrupted` / `stopped` | `read` current state first before retrying | Blindly repeating pay/send/delete/submit |
| Multi-page list / `room_note` | `browser_collect` (lists) or `browser_task` (many pages) | Reading dozens of pages inline |

## Unusual-site skills (read ONLY when visiting that site)
| Site | File | Why it is unusual |
|---|---|---|
| `gov.kr` / `plus.gov.kr` (정부24) | `references/sites/gov-kr.md` | Requires PC 1366px viewport + provider-first 간편인증 modal order |
| `naver.com` & "Sign in with NAVER" | `references/sites/naver.md` | In-app ID/PW & passkey fail; create session via QR or NAVER app first |
| `weee.com` (Weee!) | `references/sites/weee.md` | First-visit popup is a sign-in layer; transparent Google overlay button |

## Common references (read only when needed)
| File | Read when |
|---|---|
| `references/signin.md` | Complex sign-in, 2FA, identity check, or field-kind judgment |
| `references/signup.md` | User asks to create a new account (회원가입) |
| `references/blocked.md` | Blocked screen, click does nothing, or desktop/Chrome fallback needed |
| `references/tasks.md` | Purchases, reservations, banks, or saving issued documents/PDFs |
| `references/ai-keys.md` | Creating an AI provider API key (`[key:N]` reference) |
| `references/signin-rules.json` | Machine-readable host rules (`pc_view_sites`, `desktop_sites`, `naver`, `site_notes`) |

# Getting an AI Key for the Person (AI connection on their behalf)

Use when the person asks you to connect another AI ("Gemini 무료 연결해 줘", "add a free AI"), or picks [Add another AI] on a low-balance card.
The steps for each provider are data, not this document: call `ai_connection_add` with `operation: providers` and follow that provider's `key_steps` and `key_page`. If the screen differs from the steps, follow the screen.

## Choosing

- If the person named a provider, use it. Otherwise suggest the free ones first (`free: true` in the list; mention `free_terms` and whether a card is needed) and let them pick (`ask_user`).
- Already `connected: true`? Say so; only add again if they want a new key.

## Sign-in ways

| Provider kind | Way |
|---|---|
| `sign_in: true` (ChatGPT plan, OpenRouter) | No key page: call `ai_connection_add` with only `provider`. Gurum opens its sign-in page; the person approves there. Wait for the result |
| Key providers | Open `key_page` in the in-app browser (`browser`). Google consoles (AI Studio) sign in with the Google account in this browser using e-mail and **password** (NEVER passkey); if Google refuses, use a paired Mac/Windows browser or the person's Chrome (`open_url` with `app: chrome`) — see `blocked.md` |

## Steps on a key page

1. Do everything you can automatically — NEVER ask the user to copy/paste API keys, tokens, model names, or URLs manually. Only pause for user input on missing login credentials (sign-in card), 2FA/CAPTCHA (`wait_for_person`), or paid plan/billing approval.
2. Press the create-key button (often "Create API key" / "API 키 만들기"). Name it "Gurum" if a name is asked.
3. When the new key/token is shown on screen, the tool result masks it as a reference like `[key:1]` — immediately register it yourself with `ai_connection_add(operation: "add", provider: ..., key: "[key:1]", model: ...)`.
4. If the page hides the key/token and offers a Copy button (or Reveal/eye button): YOU press the Copy button in the in-app browser yourself, then immediately call `ai_connection_add` with `clipboard: true` (and `provider` / `model`) so Gurum reads the copied token directly from the clipboard and finishes registration automatically! (In external Chrome where clipboard cannot be read in background, press the reveal/eye button so `[key:1]` is captured.)
5. The result says `connected`, the model chosen and its place in the order (free ones are used first). Tell the person in one short line. On an error, relay it plainly (wrong key, no credit) and offer another way.

## Do not

- Type, repeat, or put a key in a message, memory, file, or search.
- Turn on paid features, top up, or change billing without the person's request and the payment approval card.
- Delete or rotate existing keys on the provider site, and NEVER call `settings__ai_connections(operation: "remove")` during AI setup, free-AI registration, model switching, or error recovery (use `operation: "set"` with `value: "model:<id>"` to change a model, or `operation: "add"` to add another connection).

# When Blocked

## Screens shown instead of the site

| Screen | Response |
|---|---|
| Security check ("Just a moment", "セキュリティ検証") | Wait a few seconds and `read` again. If still present, hand over to the user |
| Human-check wall (CAPTCHA, "Press & Hold"), "Access Denied" | Give `[브라우저 판 열기](<open_browser>)` so the user solves it directly |
| One-line "403 Forbidden" | May be a region/IP restriction; report plainly |
| HTTP 429, maintenance notice | Do not repeat; relay wording and suggest retrying later |
| Timeout ("The site sent nothing back") | At most one retry, then report site unresponsive |
| "Mobile not supported", "Install security program", "Unsupported browser" | Offer paired Mac/Windows computer (if available) or another method |
| Google sign-in blocked ("disallowed_useragent" / "not secure") | Offer another sign-in method on that site, connected Gmail/Calendar tools, paired Mac/Windows browser, or phone Chrome (`open_url` with `app: chrome`). Never choose passkey |

- Check/block screens are short; a long page mentioning those words is not a block.
- Some sites restrict only guest views — sign in and retry. For public info blocked on detail pages, try `web_search`/`web_url_read` first.

## When clicking changes nothing

| Cause | Response |
|---|---|
| Cookie/privacy/notice/ad overlay | Proactively auto-accept required cookies/notices or close ads (`X`, `닫기`, `오늘 그만 보기`, `나중에`) yourself without asking, then click again (leave optional/marketing unchecked) |
| Transparent shield / loading spinner | Scroll slightly or wait and `read` again; do not spam-click |
| Alert dialog | Read text; confirm ordinary notices, get approval for irreversible confirmations |
| Passkey dialog | Switch to a non-passkey method |
| Stale popup or wrong element clicked | Close leftover popup, `read` again, or click by coordinates from screenshot |
| Direct deep-step URL error | Navigate from the site's home page |

## Alternatives when the in-app browser is blocked

1. **Paired Mac or Windows computer** (when online & permitted): desktop browser / `device_action` often passes desktop-only or wide-layout checks cleanly without disturbing the user's cursor.
2. **User's Chrome on phone**: `open_url` with `url` and `app: chrome`. Gurum does not tap/type inside Chrome (Play policy) — give one short line of what to do and call `wait_for_person`. If Chrome autofill is off (`autofill: off`), offer `open_settings` page `chrome_autofill`.
3. **Report plainly**: If still blocked, state the site's exact message and offer concrete choices (`ask_user`): another sign-in way, user completes only that step via `[브라우저 판 열기]`, or a paired device.

# Sign-in and Identity Check

## Entry and methods

- Enter via the sign-in link or account icon. It is normal for the sign-in screen to be at another company's address (shared account, sign-in with another company's account).
- Click buttons that expand methods ("More options", "SNSでログイン") first and check all methods. Forgot password, sign-up, and help are not methods.
- When the user specifies a sign-in method or asks to use a different method than last time (e.g. "카카오톡으로 로그인", "아이디로 로그인"), call `sign_in` with `choose_way: true` and write the chosen method in `reason` so any previously remembered "don't ask again" method is not silently reused.
- In Korean simple authentication (간편인증 — 정부24, 홈택스, 건강보험 등), first open "간편인증", click the chosen provider icon in the provider list and confirm it is highlighted/selected, and only then fill the user's own details (`name`, `birthdate`, `phone`), check required consent ("전체동의"), and press "인증 요청". Never mix simple-auth personal details with the site's ID/password form.
- If another company's account is chosen (e.g. Google, Kakao, Apple), proceed directly on that company's screen using its saved/standard password sign-in (NEVER passkey) — do not redundantly ask the user to pick a method again unless genuinely blocked or ambiguous.
- A sign-in screen reached from a sub-service may offer fewer methods than the main sign-in screen. If the intended method is missing, go to the site's front page and enter its main sign-in screen to find it. Do not substitute another method.
- If the site blocks the chosen method as "not available in this environment", drop that method and ask again.
- NEVER choose passkey on ANY site (neither Google nor any other site). If a site shows a passkey dialog or passkey screen first, click "Try another way" / "다른 방법 시도" / "Use password" / "비밀번호 입력" and proceed with password or another non-passkey method, and always skip any post-login passkey creation offer.
- "Sign in with Google" (and any sign-in on accounts.google.com) goes on in this browser with the user's Google e-mail and **password** (NEVER passkey). Ask for credentials via the normal sign-in card if not saved in the vault. If Google still refuses, see `blocked.md`.
- Some sites only work in this browser through a fixed set of ways that make a sign-in session first (a QR code, the site's own app on this phone) — see the per-site exception files under `references/sites/` (e.g., `references/sites/naver.md`, `references/sites/gov-kr.md`). Make that session with the way the user picks, then go back to the original sign-in (the same service page, or the other site's "Sign in with <that company>" again).

## Judging fields

- Read the field's label and type and judge what it requires. Gray example text means an empty field.
- Sign-in fields that are not ID/password (branch number, account number, member number, contract number) are values specific to that site. They are not fields requiring the user's own details (name, date of birth, ID number).
- **CAPTCHA vs OTP (`code`)**: An on-page image CAPTCHA / security text (`자동등록방지 보안문자`, `자동입력방지 문자`, `보안문자`, `画像認証`, `图形验证码`, `CAPTCHA`, or a text box paired with refresh/audio buttons) is NEVER a one-time OTP `code` — it is ALWAYS a human-only `captcha` step (`then_person: "captcha"` or `person: "captcha"`). Use `code` ONLY for a one-time code actually sent via SMS/e-mail or generated by an authenticator app, and never ask for a `code` before pressing a `"인증번호 발송"` / `"Send code"` button.
- On a screen showing only the ID, the password or verification code comes on the screen after the ID.
- If one item is split across several fields or dropdown lists (year/month/day), map them in screen order.
- Auto-check terms required for sign-in (`필수 동의`, `필수 약관`) and proceed without asking; leave optional/marketing items (`선택`, `마케팅`, `광고`) unchecked. A new sign-up the user did not ask for is asked first; when the user asked to sign up, follow `signup.md`.

## Identity check

- The site may require an identity check before or after sign-in (registered date of birth, registered name, phone number, etc.).
- If there are several identity-check means and one can be completed directly with saved/known account info (e.g. password, email/SMS OTP, birthdate/name), judge and proceed automatically; ask the user only when choosing between external human-only auth apps (e.g. Kakao/PASS/Toss).
- The details registered with an account belong to that account (an account in a family member's name, an account registered with an old address/number). If no value was received for that account, do not fill in the user's own details; ask.
- The engine stores received values for that account. A shared account is one unit. The user's own details do not change.
- If the site does not accept a value, ask again. The new value replaces that account's stored value.
- The registered notation may differ (kanji/kana/romaji, name order). Relay the screen's fields and notice as is so the user enters the right notation.

## Rejection

- Rejection is the site stating in a sentence that the value is wrong, prompting a password reset, or locking the account. A field label, an echoed ID, or an additional verification/identity check screen is not rejection.
- On rejection, relay the site's wording as is and ask again. If it repeats, warn of the risk of account lockout.
- If only the sign-in screen returns with no message, retry once. If it returns again, ask the user.

## User steps

- **Do what you can first, hand off ONLY the human step**: When a login form mixes automatable fields (saved ID/password, personal details, required checkboxes) with a human-only check (image CAPTCHA, shuffled keypad), fill the automatable fields FIRST without submitting (`then_person: "captcha" | "keypad"`), then hand the browser to the user so they only complete that check.
- QR, app approval, CAPTCHA, and a shuffled picture keypad are done by the user directly (leave to the engine what the engine handles on its behalf).
- Relay the number to choose in the app exactly as on screen. A countdown is not that number.
- If the QR/approval screen disappears, judge from the screen whether it succeeded or expired. If the site has a done button after the user finishes on the phone, click it.

## Success judgment

- It is a success only when the user's account (name, member number, sign-out button) is visible on the screen of the site being signed in to. An account shown in another tab or on the screen of a company moved to is not success.
- After signing in on a shared account's or another company's screen, it is a success once the browser returns to the site originally intended and the account is visible there. Do not go back to check the company that hosted the sign-in screen.
- Even if the sign-in function ends as "unfinished", the user is signed in when the account is visible on the intended site. Do not sign in again; continue the original task.
- Do not repeat the same judgment on the same screen. If the screen does not change, stop and judge by the current state.
- Skip optional offers right after sign-in (app install, password change suggestion).
- Close windows opened by a sign-in that did not succeed.

# Signing up for a site (creating an account)

When the user asks to sign up for a site (회원가입), **complete the sign-up yourself** in the in-app browser — do not tell the user to do it themselves or stop at describing the form.

1. Open the site's sign-up page ("회원가입 / Sign up / Join"). If the user specified a method (e.g. Google or email) or has an obvious connected Google account for a service they asked you to set up, proceed directly; ask (`ask_user`) only when social vs. email sign-up is genuinely ambiguous.
2. Fill reusable personal details from memory/vault (`name`, `email`, `phone`, `birthdate`, `address`) via the sign-in/fill flow — ask only for what is missing.
3. **Password**: Let the host generate a strong password and store it in the vault for this site — never ask the user to type one and never reuse another site's password.
4. **Terms**: Auto-check **required** terms/privacy consents (`필수 동의`, `필수 약관`) and proceed without asking. Leave **optional** items (`선택`, marketing, ads, promotional SMS/push, third-party sharing) unchecked unless the user explicitly requested them.
5. **Verification**: Request SMS/email OTP or app identity check; fetch OTP from mail/notifications or ask via code card, and hand app biometric/PIN approval to the user (`phone-use/references/apps/korean-auth.md`).
6. **Final submit** ("가입하기 / Create account"): When the user explicitly asked to sign up for this site and there is **no payment or paid plan**, submit and complete the signup directly without redundant confirmation. If a paid plan/payment is involved or the user did not ask to create a new account, get approval first. Confirm on the completion screen.
7. Report: site, ID/email used, password saved to vault, optional terms left off, then continue the user's original goal.

If the site blocks this browser outright ("Access Denied"), offer the alternatives in `references/blocked.md` (paired Mac/Windows computer, user's Chrome, or the service's app).

# Government24 (`gov.kr` / `plus.gov.kr`)

- **Live domain & redirect (`2026-11`)**: `https://www.gov.kr` redirects main civil-service and sign-in flows to **`https://plus.gov.kr`** (`정부24+`, sign-in at `https://plus.gov.kr/login/login/`). For `주민등록표 등본(초본) 발급`, search or open the service directly on `plus.gov.kr`, click **"발급하기"**, and proceed to sign-in.
- **Why unusual**: Mobile web overlays an uncloseable app-only notice ("이 기능은 정부24 앱에서만 사용가능합니다"), and the simple-authentication (간편인증) modal on `plus.gov.kr` clips off narrow phone viewports.
- **Host handling**: On phones, the host automatically opens `gov.kr` / `www.gov.kr` / `plus.gov.kr` in 1366px Windows Chrome PC view (`references/signin-rules.json` `pc_view_sites`). If the app-only notice still appears, never press "앱 실행" on your own — ask the user.
- **Automated sign-in first (including "로그인 본인 인증은 내가 할게")**: When the user says "로그인 본인 인증은 내가 할게" (meaning they will approve the phone-app biometric/PIN verification), **Gurum MUST still run the full sign-in flow automatically** via `browser(action="sign_in")` on **THIS** device: open **간편인증**, click the chosen provider icon, fill the user's `name`/`birthdate`/`phone` from the vault, tick **전체동의**, and press **인증 요청** — pausing ONLY for the user's phone-app approval (`phone` step), then pressing **인증 완료**. NEVER immediately dump a manual `[브라우저 열기]` card before attempting sign-in unless the user explicitly said they will type the entire login manually in the browser ("내가 직접 로그인할게"). Never delegate `browser` / `sign_in` to another paired device unless the user explicitly named that device.
- **Security / anti-bot screen**: If `plus.gov.kr` shows a security wait or verification screen (such as `/mbuster/`), never attempt to bypass or loop; hand off cleanly to the user via `[브라우저 열기]` so they complete it in the browser pane and continue.
- **Simple authentication (간편인증) order** (when Gurum fills it):
  1. Press **"간편인증"** to open the modal.
  2. **Click the chosen provider icon in the left list FIRST** (카카오톡, 네이버, 통신사PASS, 토스, 신한인증서, KB국민인증서, 삼성패스, etc.) and confirm it is highlighted before filling any field.
  3. Fill the right-side personal details (`name`, `birthdate` 8 digits `YYYYMMDD`, `phone` `010` + 8 digits — `account: false`), check **"전체동의"** (required terms), and press **"인증 요청"**.
  4. Wait for the user's phone app approval (`phone_notifications` / `wait_for_person`), then press **"인증 완료"** back in the browser.
- **Do not mix credentials**: Never enter phone/personal details into "아이디 로그인", and never enter ID/password into "간편인증".

# NAVER (`naver.com` and "Sign in with NAVER")

Applies to all NAVER services (NAVER Shopping, Smart Store, Booking, Place, …) and third-party "Sign in with NAVER" buttons. Driven by `references/signin-rules.json` (rule `naver`).

- **In-app ID/password and passkey fail**: Do not type them or offer them on your own (NAVER rejects valid values in embedded browsers and retries can lock the account). Exception: if the vault already holds NAVER ID/password and the user explicitly chooses "saved sign-in" on the host's way card, follow it once; if rejected, offer QR or NAVER app instead of retrying.
- **Create a NAVER session first** using the user's choice:
  1. **QR code**: open `https://nid.naver.com/nidlogin.login?mode=form&url=<return_url>` → click **"QR 코드 로그인"** → relay the displayed number so the user scans and taps that number in the NAVER app on another screen.
  2. **NAVER app** (when installed on this phone): open `https://nid.naver.com/nidlogin.login?mode=form&svctype=262144&url=<return_url>` → click **"앱 열기"** beside "네이버 앱으로 자동 로그인" → user confirms in the NAVER app and returns → page advances automatically.
- **Return to the original site**: Sub-service login forms often show only ID/PW/passkey; always use the `nid.naver.com` URLs above with `<return_url>` set to the originating page or OAuth authorize page. If OAuth does not redirect automatically, reopen the target site and press "Sign in with NAVER" once more.
- **Success check**: Confirm signed-in state on the target site, not only on `nid.naver.com`.

# Weee! (`weee.com`)

# Learning Coach

Teach, assess, adapt and resume across conversations with the `learning` tool. The records live on this phone and are the same in **every**
conversation — the assistant room, topic conversations, scheduled runs and live voice all read and write the same courses. This skill is
English; learner-facing text is in the learner's chosen explanation language.

## Every learning reply

- Use `profile.explanation_language` for feedback, instructions and translations; keep the language being learned separate. Answering in the
  target language does **not** change the explanation language. Keep the requested locale and script (Traditional vs Simplified Chinese).
  Infer neither language nor timezone from nationality. Ask an unclear preference once; change it only on request (`start` again or a
  profile change).
- For a short session give one specific feedback point and one next task. Correct errors before raising difficulty; after a success, vary
  the situation. Clarify uncertain meaning or speech recognition. Unrelated messages are not answers — do not grade them.
- Grade against the saved `expected`, `rubric` and `max_score` (they come back as `pending_question_private`). Accept valid alternatives;
  tell hints from independent work. Never put the next answer key or rubric in the reply.
- Show the receipt's `reply` as it is when it has one (it is the feedback plus the next saved question). Do not narrate routine saving.

## Fast path

1. **Entry** (new conversation, "이어서 하자", after a summary, a scheduled lesson): `learning(operation:"list")` if the course is unknown, then
   `learning(operation:"state", course)`. An empty list = a new learner → **Start** below.
2. **One answer = one call**, with the grade and `advance`:

```json
{"operation":"answer","course":"english-conversation","request_id":"msg-41","answer":"I'd like a coffee, please.",
 "grade":{"score":1,"assistance":"none","feedback":"좋아요! 'I'd like ~, please' 는 정중한 주문이에요."},"advance":"auto"}
```

   This is a format example, not learner data. `advance:"auto"` moves to the next prepared question only on full credit, otherwise keeps
   the same task; choose `stay`, `next`, `finish`, or a new activity (`next` / `next_lesson` + `reply`) when the learner needs it.
3. Prepare **about three short questions** per lesson while the topic is stable — do not invent a new question on every success. At the
   last prepared question, if study continues, replace `advance` with `next_lesson` (a few new tasks) and `reply` presenting the first.
4. Use a stable `request_id` (the user's message is one event); retry a lost call with the **same** id and input — it returns
   `already_saved` instead of saving twice. A `saved` receipt confirms persistence; do not read again to check.

Field details, other operations and examples: `references/operations.md`.

## Start

Ask only the missing essentials: subject/goal, current level (self-reported), session length, a deadline if any. Then one
`start` with a small provisional plan (objectives with `success_criteria`) and about three short questions with complete `expected` answers
and rubrics. Store each learner-facing prompt in the explanation language, with target-language examples as needed. Do not save greeting
chatter or a full curriculum. On first use tell the learner once that study records stay on this phone (they are part of Gurum's backup).

## Judgment

- Keep coverage, independent performance and retention apart. The tool never promotes mastery by itself; `independent` needs two different
  tasks passed without help (80%+ by default), `retained` also a later success at least a day apart — if the evidence is short the receipt
  says so in `mastery_held`. Report sample size and uncertainty, never invented official levels (CEFR, JLPT, TOEIC scores) or mastery
  percentages. Read `references/assessment.md` for promotion, grade challenges or detailed reports.
- Long grading or unclear speech: save the answer first (no `grade`), grade later with `operation:"grade"` and the `turn_id`. An intentional
  no-score is `grading_status: withheld|skipped` with a reason. A mistaken grade is fixed with `operation:"correct"` (the original stays).
- Stable topics: reliable model knowledge. Changing or uncertain facts (exam formats, rules, versions): `web_search` / `web_url_read` first and
  keep the source URL and date in the lesson's `sources`.
- Choose text or voice activities from the learner's goals, observed difficulties and preferences — no fixed language-to-exercise rule, no
  forced repetition every lesson. Store the chosen `activity` (`{kind, input_mode, assessment_focus}`) with its question.

## Voice, daily lessons and other conversations

Read `references/voice-and-schedule.md` when the learner talks by live voice, asks for a daily lesson ("매일 10분 영어"), or continues a
course in another conversation. In short:

- **Live voice**: the voice model hands the learner's words to this assistant; your answer is read aloud as a short summary. Keep replies
  speakable (one feedback point + one question, no tables), save answers with `modality:"voice"`. Only the transcript is available — never
  score pronunciation; grade meaning, words and grammar.
- **Daily lesson**: only when the learner asked for one, or said yes to your offer (`ask_user`: whether, then what time) — the time is theirs, never one
  you pick. Then `schedule_job(operation:"save", title:"영어 회화 10분", time:"20:00", instruction:"learning-coach 스킬을 읽고 learning state 로 english-conversation 과정의 다음 질문 하나를 짧게 내 줘", user_request:"<their words>")`.
  Saved review dates do not notify anyone by themselves — only a scheduled job does.

Check the reply's language, script/locale, correctness and that no solution leaked before sending it.

# Assessment and Mastery

Read when designing an assessment, grading responses, or updating mastery. These are operational defaults to adapt to the actual subject and learner's goals.

## Choose the assessment purpose

| Purpose | Design | Interpretation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| diagnosis | Representative tasks exploring the starting point | Provisional strengths and gaps, not an official level |
| practice | Hints, examples, and guided steps allowed | Evidence of learning and misconceptions; distinguish from independence |
| checkpoint | New tasks under stated assistance conditions | Evidence of independent performance |
| review | Tasks testing the same ability after a delay | Evidence of retention and transfer |

Map each item to objective IDs. Establish expected answers, acceptable alternatives, a rubric, and difficulty before receiving the response. Preserve the rubric version. Avoid treating a single task as a complete assessment of a broad subject.

Set `max_score` when preparing a question (default 1). Grading reuses that maximum; a different `grade.max_score` after the answer is ignored (the receipt notes it). Keep feedback in the learner's explanation language and judge the response against the target-language task; a target-language answer does not change the explanation preference.

## Grade fairly

- For objective items, distinguish exact answers from acceptable semantic alternatives. Do not penalize spelling unless it is part of the target ability.
- For explanations and calculations, evaluate relevant reasoning, assumptions, procedure, and outcome. Explain partial credit.
- For language production, use relevant dimensions such as task completion, meaning, grammar, and vocabulary. Accept valid alternative expressions.
- Do not infer pronunciation or listening ability from text-only tasks. State what can be assessed with the available modalities.
- For specialist subjects, verify answers that depend on version, jurisdiction, or assumptions. Withhold grading for unsupported or ambiguous items.
- Use `score: null` for skipped, unanswered, ambiguous, or ungraded items and exclude them from the scoring denominator. Mark intentional no-score decisions as `grading_status: withheld` or `skipped`, with `grading_reason`. Only `pending` stays in the work queue; null without a status defaults to pending. Do not silently turn missing responses into wrong answers.
- Record assistance per item as `none`, `hint`, `solution_seen`, or `unknown`. Do not guess when unknown.
- If the learner challenges a grade, recheck the evidence and rubric. Save mistakes as a `correction` without destroying the original response or grade.

## Objective states

Track coverage and mastery separately.

| Dimension | Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| coverage | not_started | Not studied yet |
| coverage | in_progress | Teaching or practice in progress |
| coverage | covered | Planned learning activities completed |
| mastery | unassessed | No adequate assessment evidence |
| mastery | developing | Partial success; assistance, errors, or further checks remain |
| mastery | independent | Evidence meets the objective's success criteria without assistance |
| mastery | retained | Success criteria met independently again after a meaningful delay |

- Specify success criteria in the plan, such as selecting and explaining an appropriate statistical test in two different scenarios.
- Collect representative independent evidence proportional to the objective's breadth and consequence. One correct response supports a narrow observation; disclose limited samples.
- Retention requires earlier evidence, a real elapsed interval, and later independent success. Time passing alone or repeating an exposed answer immediately does not establish it.
- Cite assessment record IDs (from `report`) and explain each judgment. Consider contrary evidence without overreacting to one mistake.
- Show the last verification date for old evidence and recommend a recheck. Do not declare that the learner has forgotten solely because time passed.
- These states describe performance observed in this learning track. Do not automatically convert them to CEFR, JLPT, professional certification, or pass probabilities.

The `learning` tool keeps a mechanical minimum for `independent` and `retained`: two distinct tasks passed independently at 80% or higher by default, with a strictly positive score. Retained also requires passing observations at least one day apart. Configure an objective's `mastery_rule` (in `start` objectives) with `min_independent_items`, `pass_ratio`, and `retention_days` when the course needs another explicit policy. Repeating the same task does not increase the distinct-task count. A level the evidence does not reach is held at the highest supported one and the receipt's `mastery_held` says why. These checks are necessary conditions, not a substitute for judging stated success criteria, task equivalence, or contradictory evidence.

## Compare and report

Check plan scope, task difficulty, assistance, and rubric compatibility before comparing results. Use common objectives and comparable tasks rather than claiming improvement from a difference in unrelated total scores.

Aggregate only scored items. Separate independent results from assisted ones and state item counts. A score summary is not automatically a calibrated mastery estimate.

Example report shape:

> You have covered 3 of the current plan's 8 objectives. Today you used the past tense independently in 2 of 3 new prompts. Question word order still needs practice. We will check it again in a different situation in three days.

Use actual saved evidence in a learner report; never copy these illustrative numbers as results.

## Voice evidence and activity choice

Choose the activity and assessed ability from the learner's goal, current evidence and what this phone can actually do. Reference-speech
imitation is useful practice but is not independent generation: record `solution_seen` or the applicable assistance, and later test an
unprompted task. An immediate successful repetition does not establish retention.

On this phone a live voice conversation reaches you as **text** (the transcript of what the learner said) — there is no recording you can
listen to. So never give a pronunciation score: grade meaning, word choice and grammar under a matching rubric, and if the learner asks
about pronunciation say honestly that only the words were heard as text. A question whose `activity.assessment_focus` includes
`pronunciation` keeps its score for the words only (the tool marks the item `evidence_mode: transcript`). Transcription can be wrong:
when a strange word may be a recognition error, ask once before marking it wrong.

Do not impose an accent or lesson sequence based on nationality. Distinguish the explanation language, target speech language/accent, and
the user's chosen script/locale. You choose whether listening, repetition, role-play or a text task would help.

# learning — operations

Read `SKILL.md` first. One tool, `learning(operation, …)`. All records of a course are kept in order and never overwritten; every call
returns a receipt (`status: saved | already_saved`, `revision`, `ids`, `pending_question_id`, `pending_question_private`, optional `reply`,
`notes`). Read `notes` — they say when the tool adjusted something instead of refusing (an unknown field, a second transition, a mastery
level the evidence does not support yet).

`course` can be left out when exactly one course is saved. Use a stable short id (`english-conversation`, `japanese-travel`,
`math-fractions`); `list` before creating another.

## Read

| Call | Gives |
|---|---|
| `{"operation":"list"}` | every course: subject, goal, plan, revision, updated_at, status, the pending question's prompt |
| `{"operation":"state","course":…}` | profile, plan (current objectives), checkpoint (status, mode, next_action), lesson title (`include_lesson:true` adds the teaching text), `pending_question_private` (prompt, expected, rubric, max_score — **coach only**), last answer, current progress, queues of ungraded/withheld/skipped answers |
| `{"operation":"report","course":…,"recent":10}` | objectives with coverage/mastery/next review/evidence count, score totals split by assistance (independent · assisted · unknown), recent graded items with feedback, lesson list |

## Start — one request

```json
{"operation":"start","course":"english-conversation","request_id":"msg-12",
 "profile":{"subject":"English conversation","goal":"Order food and ask simple questions on a trip","explanation_language":"ko-KR",
            "target_language":"en-US","self_reported_level":"beginner","session_minutes":10},
 "objectives":[{"id":"order-food","label":"Order food politely","success_criteria":"Order politely in two different situations without hints"}],
 "lesson":{"title":"Ordering at a café","content":"주문할 때는 'I'd like ~, please.' 가 정중해요. 예: I'd like a latte, please.",
   "questions":[
     {"id":"q1","prompt":"카페에서 아이스 아메리카노 한 잔을 정중하게 주문해 보세요.","expected":"I'd like an iced americano, please. (or an equivalent polite request)","rubric":"1 point for a comprehensible polite order","difficulty":"introductory"},
     {"id":"q2","prompt":"사이즈를 물으면 '큰 걸로요'라고 답해 보세요.","expected":"A large one, please. / Large, please.","rubric":"1 point for a comprehensible size answer","difficulty":"introductory"},
     {"id":"q3","prompt":"점원에게 '여기서 먹을게요'라고 말해 보세요.","expected":"For here, please. / I'll eat here.","rubric":"1 point for a comprehensible answer","difficulty":"introductory"}]},
 "reply":"좋아요, 카페 주문부터 해 볼게요. …(가르치는 글)…\n\n카페에서 아이스 아메리카노 한 잔을 정중하게 주문해 보세요."}
```

A format example, not learner data. Required: `profile.subject`, `profile.goal`, `profile.explanation_language`; each objective's `label`
and `success_criteria`; each question's `prompt`, `expected`, `rubric`. Defaults: question ids `q1…`, `max_score` 1, timezone = the phone's,
objective ids `o1…`. `title` names the plan (default: the subject). Starting an existing course again saves a **new plan on top** — earlier
evidence stays and objectives with the same id keep their state. Show your own `reply` (the receipt echoes it).

## Answer and grade — one request

```json
{"operation":"answer","course":"english-conversation","request_id":"msg-13","answer":"I want ice americano.",
 "grade":{"score":0.5,"assistance":"none","feedback":"뜻은 통해요! 'I want' 보다 'I'd like ~, please' 가 더 정중해요. 'an iced americano' 처럼 관사도 붙여 보세요."},
 "advance":"stay"}
```

- The tool copies the saved prompt, key, rubric, difficulty and objectives into the assessment — do not repeat them.
- `answer` = the learner's exact words (for voice, the transcript). `question_id` defaults to the pending question; an answer to an older
  prepared question can name it.
- `grade`: `score` (0…max — or null = not graded yet), `assistance` `none | hint | solution_seen | unknown` (do not guess), `feedback` in the
  explanation language, optional `grading_status` `scored | pending | withheld | skipped` + `grading_reason`, `purpose`
  `diagnosis | practice | checkpoint (default) | review`, `actual_prompt` if you asked it differently than saved.
- One transition at most: `advance` (`auto | next | stay | finish` — the receipt's `reply` = feedback + the next saved question) · `next`
  (one new question `{prompt, expected, rubric, …}` + your `reply` with the explanation and the question) · `next_lesson` (a full lesson +
  `reply`) · `next_question_id`. Several given → only the first of next_lesson > next > next_question_id > advance is used.
- `objective_updates: [{id, rationale, coverage?, mastery?, next_review_at?}]` — targeted changes; the new assessment is attached as
  evidence automatically. `independent` / `retained` are kept only when the saved evidence meets the plan's rule (receipt `mastery_held`
  says what is missing).
- On a misconception: targeted correction, and count hints on the next attempt (`assistance:"hint"`).

## Capture first, grade later

For unclear speech or long grading send `answer` without `grade` → the receipt gives `turn_id`. Later:

```json
{"operation":"grade","course":"english-conversation","turn_id":"turn-14","grade":{"score":1,"assistance":"none","feedback":"…"},"advance":"auto"}
```

Grading an answer that already has a grade saves a **correction** of it instead (the original stays visible in the records).
Intentional no-score: `{"score":null,"grading_status":"withheld","grading_reason":"The question was ambiguous","assistance":"unknown","feedback":"이 문제는 바꿀게요 — 점수에 넣지 않아요."}`.

## Other operations

- `lesson` — `{"operation":"lesson","lesson":{…},"reply":…}` prepares new material under the current plan; its first question becomes pending.
- `checkpoint` — `status` (`active | paused | finished`), `mode` (`text | voice`), `next_action`, `pending_question_id`; unspecified fields keep
  their position. Use it for "오늘은 여기까지" (`paused` + a resume note) or switching to voice.
- `correct` — `{"operation":"correct","target_id":"assessment-15","reason":"The learner's answer was also correct","score":1,"feedback":"…"}`
  or `"void":true`. The learner challenging a grade: recheck the saved answer and rubric first (`report`), then correct if they are right.

## Receipts and recovery

- `revision` = how many records the course has. Passing `expected_sequence` (the revision you read) is optional; if the course changed in
  between (another conversation or voice), the call still saves and `notes` says so — read `state` if unsure.
- Retry after a lost response with the same `request_id` and the same input → `already_saved` with the first receipt.
- Never claim a result was saved without a `saved` / `already_saved` receipt.

# Voice, daily lessons and several conversations

Read `SKILL.md` first.

## One record for every conversation

The `learning` records belong to the course, not to a conversation. The assistant room, any topic conversation from the 대화 menu, a
scheduled run and live voice all see the same courses, revisions and pending question. So:

- On entering learning in a conversation (or after the conversation was summarized), `list` / `state` first — the pending question and the
  last answer may come from another conversation or from voice. Continue from the saved task; give a one-line resume ("지난번엔 카페 주문
  두 번째 문제였어요").
- If "이어서 하자" fits more than one course, ask which before writing to either.
- A chat summary never replaces the records: grades, scores and progress are only what the tool returns.
- Mixed conversations: decide whether a message is an answer to the active task. Ordinary chat in the middle of a lesson is not graded
  and not saved as an answer.

## Live voice (실시간 음성 대화)

When the user talks to Gurum by live voice, the voice model sends their words here as a request (it starts with
"[실시간 음성 대화에서 맡긴 일 …]"), you do the work with your tools, and your answer is read aloud as a short summary.

- Treat the request text as the learner's answer when it answers the pending question. Save it with `modality:"voice"` (and `checkpoint
  mode:"voice"` when a whole session moves to voice).
- Write a reply that survives being spoken: one short feedback sentence and the next question, nothing else — no tables, lists, links or
  answer keys. Target-language phrases you want the learner to say go in quotes so the voice model reads them as they are.
- Only the transcript reaches you. No pronunciation score; if the transcript looks like a recognition error, ask once instead of marking
  it wrong. Partial or cut-off speech is not graded — save it without `grade` or ask the learner to say it again.
- Role-play (a café, an airport) works well by voice: keep each of your turns to one line in the target language plus, when the learner is
  a beginner, a short hint in the explanation language.

## Daily or weekly lessons

Saved review dates (`next_review_at`) are notes, not reminders. A regular lesson is saved only when the user asked for it or said yes when you
offered it: ask with `ask_user` (1) whether they want a daily lesson, then, after a yes, (2) at what time and on which days — unless they already
said. Pass their words as `user_request`. Then save a scheduled job:

```json
{"operation":"save","title":"영어 회화 10분","time":"20:00","user_request":"매일 저녁 8시에 영어 문제 하나씩 내 줘",
 "instruction":"learning-coach 스킬을 읽고 learning(operation:\"state\", course:\"english-conversation\") 로 다음 문제 하나를 짧게 내 줘. 준비된 문제가 없으면 지난 결과를 보고 짧은 레슨(문제 3개)을 learning lesson 으로 만들고 첫 문제를 내 줘."}
```

- `days:[0..6]` limits weekdays (0 = Monday). The fired run's reply is pushed to the user; their answer comes later in a conversation and is

# Proactive Life & Document Stewardship (`life-steward`)

When the user uploads, forwards, or shares any personal, household, or business document (a photo, PDF, screenshot, mail, or text), act as a thorough human Chief-of-Staff who **takes ownership**, **compares history**, **records structured data**, and **prepares the next cycle** right away.

## Absolute Operating Rules

1. **Zero passive endings.** Never finish with `"어떻게 할까요?"`, `"무엇을 도와드릴까요?"`, or `"등록해 드릴까요?"`. State clearly what you recognized, what changed versus prior records, and how you are managing the upcoming schedule/next cycle.
2. **Search history first (`knowledge_search` / `knowledge_read` / `recall` / `list_tasks`).** Before answering, check prior months or earlier entries of the same bill, contract, checkup, or child/school item.
   - If prior records exist: compute exact deltas (`전월 대비 +18,400원 (+6.9%)`, item-level spikes such as `난방비`, `전기료`, `수선유지비`) and render a `gurum-card` (`compare`) when 2+ periods or items are compared.
   - If this is the first record: state clearly that this month/record is saved as the baseline and next month's statement will be compared against it automatically.
3. **Preserve photo/PDF details via `[[note:...]]` + `[[keep:record]]`.** Image-only uploads have no raw text in background attachment extraction unless you write structured `[[note:...]]` lines. Always emit concise factual `[[note:...]]` lines with:

   - **S3 Vault rule:** Never write full bank account numbers, card numbers, national IDs, or passport numbers in replies or `[[note:...]]`; mask to last 4 digits if needed and store full secrets only in `site_credential`.

# Media Studio (entry)

Pictures, photo edits, videos and music are made with the tools `generate_image`, `generate_video` and `generate_music`; existing videos and
photos are cut, joined, captioned and set to music with `media_edit` (on the phone — free, always available). Each generate tool uses the
service and model the user connected in **Settings › AI connections › Make pictures, videos & music** — you do not pick the service; the tool
result tells you which one it used (`service`, `model`). A tool that is not offered means nothing is connected for that kind: tell the user
in one line where to connect it (Settings › AI connections › "그림·영상·음악 만들기") — do not try other ways (the browser, a web site) to make media.

Five principles:

1. **One result, show it, then ask.** Make one picture (one video, one song) per request. Make more only when the user asks for options
   ("여러 개", "골라 볼래") — then at most 2–4 in one call (`n`). Never regenerate on your own: if the result misses something, show it, say what
   is different and ask (`ask_user`: "이대로 / 다시 만들기 (바꿀 점 적기)").
2. **Ask only before costly work.** Pictures: never ask first — the defaults are fine and a picture is cheap to redo. Video: if a required
   item is missing (length, spoken line, which photo), ask once. The video tool itself shows the user a confirmation card before it starts — do not ask
   again yourself, and never state or guess a price (the card has none). Songs: ask only if the user wants to check the lyrics first.
3. **You write the prompt.** Expand the request into a full, concrete description in English (the mode references show how). Words that must
   appear on screen, spoken lines and lyrics stay exactly as the user wrote them (Korean stays Korean, letter for letter). See
   `references/providers.md` for what the connected model handles well (text in pictures, negative words, length).
4. **The result is shown automatically.** The tool attaches the files under your reply. Do not paste links, file paths or markdown images.
   Reply in one or two plain lines: what you made, and one thing they could do next ("배경만 바꾸거나 영상으로 움직이게 할 수 있어요").
5. **Check against the request, not taste.** Before reporting, look at the result with `view_attachment(name, question)` when the request had
   fixed items (exact words, counts, a person who must stay the same). Ask for the visible text verbatim and compare it yourself letter by

| I Edit | `<ep>_draft.mp4` | one `media_edit`: clips in order + captions from the script + music | card ③ |

### B–C. Characters and sheets (card ①)

- The **appearance sentence** is repeated word for word in every picture and video prompt with that character — it is what keeps them the
  same across segments and episodes. The **voice sentence** goes before their first line in each clip.
- Sheets: per character one full-body front view (`2:3`, plain light gray background, the outfit of the appearance sentence) and one head-
  and-shoulders close-up (`3:4`); plus one location (`9:16`). From a family photo: "Keep the face, identity and hairstyle exactly as in
  picture 1". Make them in one reply (`n` or several calls) — "인물 시트 N장을 한 번에 만들어요."
- Check against the photo and the sentence, then card ① — one question per character:
  `ask_user` "아빠 시트 이대로 쓸까요?" — 좋아요 / 다시 만들기 (어떻게 바꿀지 적기). Write the approved file names into the series file.

### D–E. Script and shot list (card ② — the cheapest place to change anything)

Show the script summary and a short shot table (segment · seconds · camera · action · line), then **one** `ask_user` before any video,
with the total and the number of video calls: "이 대본(영상 4개 · 30초)으로 만들까요? 영상마다 확인 카드가 떠요." — 이대로 진행 /
대사 고치기 / 줄거리 바꾸기 / 길이 바꾸기. Checks: the segments add up to the length; a line ends inside its segment; each line ≈ 2–3 s.

### F–H. Frames, clips, music

- First frame per segment: "Show <the father from picture 1> and <the daughter from picture 2> in <the living room from picture 3>: {the
  first shot's framing and action}. Keep each person's face, hair and outfit exactly as in their own picture." (image.md §B form; with a
  family photo, add the original photo too, as the same subject). Check: same people, outfits, number of people. A miss → show it and ask.
- Clip per segment (`video.md` B form): the style sentence → the shot(s) in order with camera and action → each line as
  `<appearance sentence>, in <voice sentence>, says: "아빠 뭐 숨겼어?"` (the Korean exactly; voice sentence only at the first line of that
  character in the clip) → "No subtitles, no on-screen text. No background music." Segments are made **independently from their own frames**
  and joined by cuts.
- Music: one instrumental track for the whole episode, in the tone of the series (genre, instruments, tempo words).
- Say the wait first ("영상 4개와 배경음악을 만들어요. 영상마다 몇 분씩 걸려요"). Each video call shows its confirmation card; a declined card
  stops there — ask what to change, do not retry.

### Check

Each clip: `view_attachment(clip, "Is it the same people as the sheets (face, glasses, clothes)? Does the action follow: …? Any text on screen?")`.
Lines: you cannot hear the sound — say so in one line, the user judges it. A failed segment: show it and ask whether to remake just that one.

### I. Edit (card ③)

One `media_edit`: `clips` in order (cut each to its best part with `start`/`end`), `aspect_ratio:"9:16"`, `captions` = the script's lines
in order with times on the finished video (one short line each, 1.5–3 s), `music` = the episode track with `music_volume` ~0.3 (there is
speech). Then card ③: "이 버전으로 완성할까요?" — 완성 / 조각 다시 (어느 부분을 어떻게) / 음악 바꾸기 / 자막 고치기.
"완성" → note it in the series file (episode done, a one-line summary, the ending for the next episode). A change redoes only that stage
(one segment → its clip → the edit again; music → H then I; a line → D–E → that segment → I).

## Next episode

"2화 만들자": read the series file, reuse the approved sheets and location, write the new script from the previous ending, and start at D.

## Time (say it)

Sheets about a minute · first frames about a minute · each video clip a few minutes (the service's speed) · music one to two minutes · the
edit seconds to minutes on the phone. Two or three checks with the user.

# Editing videos · short-form · dance and lip-sync

Read `SKILL.md` first. `media_edit` runs **on the phone** — free, no service, works even when nothing is connected. It writes a new video
(the originals stay). Inputs are file names of this conversation (`list_attachments`): attached videos/photos and files you made.

## A. media_edit

```text
media_edit(clips=[{file, start?, end?, seconds?}, …],      # in order; videos cut by start/end (seconds or m:ss), photos stay `seconds` (default 3)
           captions?=[{text, start, end?, position?}],       # times on the FINISHED video · position bottom (default) | middle | top
           aspect_ratio?="9:16"|"16:9"|"1:1"|"4:5"|"original", fit?="crop"|"pad",
           music?=<song file>, music_volume?=0.35, original_volume?=1, speed?=1, name?)
```

| Request | Call |
|---|---|
| "앞 3초 잘라줘" | `clips=[{file:"a.mp4", start:3}]` |
| "10초부터 20초까지만" | `clips=[{file:"a.mp4", start:10, end:20}]` |
| "이 두 영상 이어 붙여 줘" | `clips=[{file:"a.mp4"},{file:"b.mp4"}]` (different sizes are fitted to the first one's shape — or set `aspect_ratio`) |
| "사진들로 영상 만들어 줘" | `clips=[{file:"1.jpg",seconds:2.5},…]` + usually `aspect_ratio:"9:16"` and `music` |
| "자막 넣어 줘" | `captions=[{text:"…", start:0, end:2.5}, …]` — the user's words exactly; one short line (≤ 16 Korean characters) per caption |
| "쇼츠용 세로로" | `aspect_ratio:"9:16"` (crop fills the screen; `fit:"pad"` keeps everything with bars) |
| "배경음악 깔아 줘" | `music:"song.mp3"` — loops or is cut to the video; `music_volume` 0.2–0.4 under speech, 0.6–0.9 with no speech; `original_volume:0` mutes the clips |
| "2배속" / "슬로모션" | `speed:2` / `speed:0.5` (sound changes pitch) |

- One call does everything at once (cut + join + captions + music). Do not chain calls when one will do.
- Caption times: plan them on the finished video (after cuts and speed). Spread lines so each stays 1.5–3 s; the next caption replaces it.
- Need to know a video's length or what happens when? `view_attachment(name, "What happens at each second? How long is it?")` first.
- Takes from seconds to a few minutes (longer and more clips = longer); the tool shows progress and keeps going if the user leaves the app.
- Report in one line what changed ("이어 붙이고 자막 4줄을 넣었어요 · 24초").

## B. Short-form (15–30 s · 쇼츠·릴스·틱톡)

Use when the user wants a short, vertical, captioned clip — from their own clips/photos, or made from scratch.

1. **Plan in words first** (no tool): the hook in the first 1–3 s (an unexpected moment, the result first, or one question), 3–8 shots of
   2–4 s, the caption lines, the music. Show the plan as a short list and ask once with `ask_user` only when you would make **new videos**
   (they cost money): "이대로 / 바꿀 점".
2. **Material**:
   - The user's own clips/photos → go straight to step 3.
   - New pictures → `generate_image` (cheap; one reply can make several with `n`, 9:16).
   - New video shots → `generate_video` (9:16; 4–8 s each). Each call shows its own confirmation card — keep the number of new video shots small
     (2–3) and fill the rest with photos/pictures.
   - Music → the user's song, or `generate_music` (instrumental, the total length).
3. **Assemble with one `media_edit`**: clips in order (cut each to its best 2–4 s with start/end), `aspect_ratio:"9:16"`, captions on the
   hook and key beats, `music` with `music_volume` ~0.35 (≈0.8 if the clips have no speech), `original_volume` 0 if the clips' own sound is noise.
4. Check one frame or two with `view_attachment` (captions readable, not covering faces). Report in one line.

Captions for short-form: big, few words, bottom (default) or `middle` for the hook. Never caption a song's lyrics unless asked.

More for short-form (from the engine's shortform-trend recipe):

- One template that is a single clip of 15 s or less (a dance challenge, a hug) needs only `trends.md`; this recipe is for 2+ segments or
  editing with captions and music. A story with recurring characters is `drama.md`.
- The plan card, when new videos will be made: "30초 · 영상 3개 · 사진 4장 · 배경음악으로 만들까요?" — 이대로 진행 / 훅 바꾸기 (첫 장면을
  어떻게) / 15초로 줄이기 / 다시 기획.
- New video shots: make each shot's first frame as a picture first (`generate_image`, 9:16 — cheap) and check it; then animate that frame
  (`first_frame`). Repeat the same style sentence and the same description of each person/animal (a visual anchor such as the same cap and
  jacket) in every shot's prompt, and end a spoken line inside its own shot.
- Music: a challenge's original song when the user gives it; otherwise one instrumental track for the whole length. Hook caption only
  when the user wants one; spoken lines are captioned from the words you wrote.
- After assembling, ask once: "이 버전으로 완성할까요?" — 완성 / 조각 다시 (어느 부분을 어떻게) / 음악 바꾸기 / 자막 고치기. A change
  redoes only that part and assembles again.

## C. Dance copy and lip-sync (참조 영상)

These need a video service that takes a **reference video** — not every service does. Call `generate_video` with the references; if no
connected service can, the result says so with the service to connect: tell the user in one line and offer what works instead (§B with a
photo animated from words + music).

| Request | Call |
|---|---|
| "우리 아이가 이 춤 추게" (photo + dance video) | `generate_video(prompt, first_frame:"kid.jpg", reference_video:"dance.mp4")` — the person in the photo copies the moves |
| "이 영상 속 사람이 이 노래 부르게" (face video + song/voice) | `generate_video(prompt, reference_video:"face.mp4", reference_audio:"song.mp3")` — lips follow the sound |

- First cut the reference to just the part needed (`media_edit` start/end): shorter = cheaper and faster, and large files are refused.
  Dance: up to about 10–15 s. Lip-sync: the length of the sound.
- The service charges per second of the reference — the user confirms on a card before anything is made.
- The prompt: one sentence about the scene and style ("a child dancing in a bright living room, smooth natural motion"); the moves come
  from the video.
- Safety (`SKILL.md` §4): only the **moves** of a celebrity's dance video are used — never their face or body; do not make a real public
  figure appear to sing or speak. Children: family-friendly dances only.
- Want the original song on the result? Add it after with `media_edit(music:…, original_volume:0, music_volume:0.9)`.

# Pictures

Read `SKILL.md` first (brief, one result, checking). This page covers writing the prompt and the `generate_image` call.

## A. From words (text to picture)

Most image models do not expand a short phrase well — write the whole scene. One English paragraph, present tense, about 8–20 sentences
(shorter for simple icons). Order:

1. **Fixed and open items** — exact text letter for letter (spaces and punctuation too). Work instructions ("4K", "선명하게") are not content:
   do not write them into the prompt (at most `quality: "high"` when the user asks for best quality).
2. **Ratio** — what the user said; otherwise wide scene `3:2`, tall portrait `2:3`, icon/badge/album cover `1:1`, wallpaper/banner `16:9`,
   phone screen/vertical banner `9:16`. Put it in `aspect_ratio`, not in the prompt.
3. **First sentence (~20 words)** — medium, style, subject, setting/palette: `A wide photorealistic photograph of …`, `A flat vector
   illustration of …`, `A soft watercolor painting of …`.
4. **List first** — 8–14 elements and where each is; every readable text in reading order.
5. **Walk the frame** — a scene: background → top → left/center/right → bottom. One subject (person, object): background → pose/position →
   face → body/clothes → what they hold → edges. Start about a third of the sentences with a place word ("Across the top…", "In the lower-left corner…").
6. **Text** — position, shape, weight, color, and the exact words in straight double quotes: `a cream wooden sign across the top reads
   "해피베이커리" in large rounded dark-brown letters`. A second line is a second phrase ("a second line below reads …"). Small text that must
   not be readable: "blurred, too small to read". Do not invent signs for pictures that need no text.
7. **Lighting** — one sentence: `The lighting is …` (source, direction, softness, shadows).
8. **Finish** — one sentence: `The overall composition …` (balance, palette, mood).

Style: colors with modifiers (deep navy, warm terracotta), materials, ages as "in her thirties", kinds instead of brand names. No
"masterpiece, 8K, highly detailed". Describe what should be there instead of "no …/without …" (most models have no negative prompt and a
negative word tends to appear) — unless `providers.md` says the connected model handles exclusions.

**Korean things — spell out what they are made of.** A name alone comes out wrong: 된장찌개 = `a small black earthenware pot of bubbling brown
soybean-paste stew with cubes of white tofu, sliced zucchini and green chili`; 김치 = `a small white dish of napa cabbage kimchi, pale cabbage
leaves coated in red chili paste`. Bowls, ingredients, colors, how it is served.

**Text in pictures** — keep it short (a sign or title or two, each under about 10 characters works best). Long sentences often come out with
wrong letters; if the user wants a long text, write it exactly and check it strictly (`view_attachment` → visible text verbatim → compare).

Example — "우리 빵집 '해피베이커리' 간판 달린 아침 가게 그림":

```text
generate_image(aspect_ratio="3:2", prompt="A wide warm photorealistic photograph of a small neighborhood bakery at early morning, seen from
across a quiet sidewalk under a pale blue sky. Behind the storefront, the upper floors of a cream brick building fade into soft morning haze.
Across the top of the storefront, a cream-colored wooden sign reads \"해피베이커리\" in large rounded dark-brown letters, with a small painted
wheat sprig to its left. Below the sign, a wide glass window shows three rows of golden croissants, round country loaves and braided buns on
weathered wooden shelves. To the left of the window, a pale green door with a brass handle stands half open, a small bell above it. In the
lower-left corner, a chalkboard easel stands on the pavement, its handwriting blurred and too small to read. On the right, two wrought-iron
chairs and a small round marble table sit beside a potted olive tree. Along the bottom edge, pale gray paving stones run horizontally, a few
yellow leaves scattered across them. A striped olive-and-cream awning casts a soft shadow over the right half of the window. The lighting is
soft low sunlight from the right, casting long gentle shadows and warming the sign and the bread. The overall composition is balanced and
inviting, with a warm cream, olive and golden-brown palette and a calm, freshly baked morning mood.")
```

Check: `view_attachment(name, "List every readable text exactly as written, in reading order. How many signs, people, cats? Any malformed hands or faces?")` —
compare the text yourself; if "해피베이커리" came out different, show it and ask whether to try again.

## B. With reference photos (edit · restyle · combine · new picture of the same subject)

Every call with `source_images` follows this — fixing a photo, and also making a new scene, sticker or figure of the person, pet or object in
the photos. Only works when the connected model can edit (the tool says if it cannot — then tell the user which service in AI connections can).

Three ideas:

1. **The photo carries the look; the words say only what changes.** Re-describing the face or fur competes with the photo and gives a
   different face. Name each subject just enough to find it, then refer to it by that name.
2. **No negative words.** "no glasses" tends to draw glasses. Write the final state of that place instead ("the tabletop continues
   uninterrupted where the cup stood").
3. **Everything visible in the reference comes along** — clothes, stickers, filters, stains. If the result must not have something, use a
   photo without it, or ask the user for a better photo.

Steps:

1. **Look first** — `view_attachment(name, "Who/what is where, how large the main subject is, face directions, anything covering it,
   background, every readable text verbatim, medium (photo/drawing/scan).")`.
2. **Choose references** — only the user's own originals carry identity (an earlier generated picture is a base to fix, not proof of who it
   is). 1–3 photos per subject, each with a role (close face + full body). Subject large, sharp and uncovered. If none is usable, say so and
   ask for a better photo before making anything.
3. **Which kind** — *fix this picture* (local change, background, text, style, ratio): base = that picture; say exactly what changes, the rest
   stays. *New picture of this subject* (new scene, composite, poster, character sheet): design the scene freely, keep the identity.
4. **Prompt — one paragraph in this order:**
   - **Define** each subject from its picture, numbered by the order in `source_images` (1 = first): `The small white dog in picture 1 and in
     picture 2 is subject 1.` `The woman on the left in picture 1 is subject 2.` Only kind + position + one or two visible cues. Same subject in
     several photos: name each photo. Text that must stay: define it with the text read from the photo in quotes once.
   - **Target and relation** — `The target image …` in one or two sentences, and a relation for every subject:
     fully preserved (`Subject 1 is fully preserved.` — only if pose, place and light do not change) · partly preserved (`Subject 1 is partly
     preserved; its identity, face, coat and proportions remain while its pose and surroundings change.`) · lends a property (`Subject 2
     supplies the exact body color for subject 1.`) · weak style reference.
     What remains, by kind: person `identity, facial features, hairstyle` (+ `outfit` if it stays) · animal `identity, face, coat, markings and
     proportions` · object `shape, material, color and printed details`. Style change only: `…remain while the depiction changes from
     photograph to watercolor illustration.`
   - **Only what changes or is new, in detail** — the final state, not commands ("Behind subject 1 a bright sandy beach extends to a calm
     turquoise sea", not "replace the background"). Do not re-describe what is preserved. New text: exact words in quotes; "No other lettering
     is added." when nothing else may appear. Never write words like blemish, stain, scar — describe the wanted final look of that area.
   - English for the description; on-picture text as the user gave it.
   - Some services want their own reference wording (e.g. `<Picture 1>` / `image 1` / `@image1`) — see `providers.md`; the plain "picture 1"
     form above works for the rest.
5. **Ratio** — leave `aspect_ratio` out to keep the photo's shape; give it only when the user wants another shape.

Example — "우리 강아지 사진(1번)으로 바닷가에서 뛰는 그림":

```text
generate_image(source_images=["dog.jpg"], aspect_ratio="3:2", prompt="The small white dog in picture 1 is subject 1. The target image is a
bright photorealistic beach scene of subject 1 running along the shore. Subject 1 is partly preserved; its identity, face, coat, markings and
proportions remain while its pose and surroundings change. Subject 1 runs toward the camera with ears flying and front paws lifted, wet sand
splashing behind. Behind it a wide sandy beach meets a calm turquoise sea under a clear morning sky, small waves breaking in white lines.
The lighting is low golden sunlight from the left with soft long shadows. The overall composition is lively, with subject 1 large in the
center-left and a fresh blue-and-sand palette.")
```

Check: look at the original and the result separately — first the original ("list the features that tell this individual apart: face shape,
eyes, nose, ears, coat color and markings"), then the result against that list (same / different / cannot tell, plus anything the original
does not have). Report what you saw; the user decides whether it is the same dog.

## Repeated edits

"조금 더 밝게", "다시" — change that line of the brief and write the prompt again from the top. To change only part of a result, use that
result as the base (`source_images` = the result's name) and keep identity from the user's original photo when a person/pet matters (put the
original in as picture 2 with "subject 1 in picture 2 carries the identity").

# Music — songs and background music

Read `SKILL.md` first. One song per request; if it misses, play it back (it is attached) and ask before making another.

## The call

```text
generate_music(prompt="<style line>", lyrics="<sections>"?, instrumental=true?, seconds=?)
```

- `prompt` = **the style line**: language, genre, main instruments, vocal character, tempo words — comma-separated:
  `Korean, bright children's pop, ukulele and hand claps, light drums, warm female vocal, upbeat`. Genre words beat numbers (a ballad stays
  slow even with "120 bpm"); one or two mood words at most.
- `lyrics` = section tags on their own lines with the words below, a blank line between sections: `[Intro]` `[Verse]` `[Pre-Chorus]`
  `[Chorus]` `[Bridge]` `[Outro]`. Only real lyrics — never notes or instructions inside lyrics. Names, dates and proper nouns exactly as the
  user wrote them.
- Background music / no singing: `instrumental: true`, no `lyrics`, and add `instrumental, no vocals` to the style line.
- `seconds` — the length the user wants; some services set the length from the lyrics (see `providers.md`). Rough guide for songs:

  | Length | Sections | Lyric lines |
  |---|---|---|
  | ~30 s | Verse 4 · Chorus 4 | 8–10 |
  | ~60 s | Verse · Chorus · Verse · Chorus | 16–20 |
  | ~90 s | Intro · Verse · Pre-Chorus · Chorus · Verse · Chorus · Outro | 26–30 |

- Korean lyrics: short lines (8–12 syllables), few English words, repeat the chorus.
- If the user gave names or a story but no lyrics, write the lyrics yourself and make it right away (show the lyrics in your reply only if
  they asked to check them first — then `ask_user` "이대로 / 고치기").

Example — "딸 서연이 생일 축하 노래":

```text
generate_music(seconds=30, prompt="Korean, bright children's pop, ukulele and hand claps, light drums, warm female vocal, upbeat",
lyrics="[Verse]\n오늘은 우리 서연이 생일\n케이크 위에 촛불이 반짝\n친구들이 모두 모였네\n두 손 모아 소원을 빌어\n\n[Chorus]\n생일 축하해 서연아\n너의 웃음이 제일 좋아\n생일 축하해 서연아\n오늘은 너의 날이야")
```

## Check

The vision model cannot hear. Report what you made (style, length, the lyrics' first line) and say you could not listen to it — ask the user
to play it and tell you what to change.

# Services and models — prompt notes

The tool result names the service (`service`) and model (`model`) it used. Find that row here and adjust how you write. Everything else in
`image.md` / `video.md` / `music.md` applies to all of them. Sources: each company's official prompt guide (links), read 2026-11-14.

## OpenAI — GPT Image (pictures only)
Guide: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/image-prompting
- Say what the picture is **for** first (product photo, ad, diagram, poster), then composition, ratio and layout limits. For complex
  pictures, separate parts: scene / subject / details / constraints.
- Visible detail: materials, lighting, colors, medium. Say `photorealistic` or `a real photograph` for photos. Camera words are hints for the
  look, not physics.
- People: framing (full body, feet included), where they look, what they hold.
- **Text**: quote the words, give place and lettering style, spell unusual words letter by letter, and add `No extra text.` Small print
  needs `quality: "high"`.
- **Edits**: "change only X" + list what must stay (identity, shape, layout, lighting, labels); say no unwanted text, logos or watermarks.
- Several reference photos: number them and give each a role (subject / style / clothes / background) and how to combine them.
- No negative-prompt field — exclusions go in the prompt as short sentences ("No watermarks."). This model handles them better than most.

## xAI — Grok Imagine (pictures and videos)
Guide: https://docs.x.ai/developers/model-capabilities/images/prompting-guide
- First sentence = the subject: what it is, its state or form, what holds it, the background — in one sentence.
- Then in this order: details and focus (material, count, camera angle) → art direction (color field, two or three props) → lighting (source,
  direction, strength) → color → composition (crop, what is sharp).
- Describe what you want ("brushed steel with fine horizontal grain", not "not shiny"). Long lists of "no …" are ignored; use a negative only
  for counts or one specific object, paired with what should be there.
- Give counts and viewpoint ("two mugs, 45-degree three-quarter view").
- Edits: write the 1–3 changes first, then one sentence that the subject, angle, crop and props stay. Starting with "keep everything" makes
  it change almost nothing. Up to 5 reference photos.
- **Video**: describe shot, camera movement, lighting and sound. From a photo, the photo is the first frame and the prompt is **what happens
  next**. It makes sound and speech — write spoken lines in quotes.

## Google — Gemini "Nano Banana" pictures · Omni video · Lyria music
Guides: https://aistudio.google.com/docs/image-generation#prompt-guide · https://aistudio.google.com/docs/omni#prompt-guide ·
https://aistudio.google.com/docs/lyria-prompt-guide
- **Describe the scene, don't list keywords.** Photographic words for realism (wide-angle shot, macro shot, low-angle perspective, lens,
  lighting), concrete detail, and the purpose ("a logo for a minimal premium skincare brand").
- Complex scenes step by step (background → foreground → small props). For changes, small steps: "Keep everything the same, but …".
- No negative field — describe the wanted state ("an empty, deserted street", not "no cars").
- Text works best when you decide the exact words first, then ask for the picture. Korean is a supported language. Several reference
  photos work well (people up to about 4, objects up to about 10 for good likeness).
- **Omni video**: for one scene say `single continuous shot, no scene cuts`. Sound in the prompt ("calm background music", "Sound design: …
  No dialogue"). Timing in plain words or `[0-5s]` timecodes. Edits short + "Keep everything else the same". English prompts work best.
  16:9 or 9:16 only.
- **Lyria music**: genre first, then instruments, BPM, key, mood and structure; `[Verse]` `[Chorus]` `[Bridge]` tags; lyrics in the wanted
  language, kept apart from instructions. Lyria 3 Clip always makes 30 seconds — good for trying an idea first.
- Not available on Gemini's free tier — if it fails with a billing message, tell the user billing must be linked in Google AI Studio.

## OpenRouter (many companies' models)
Guides: https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/overview/multimodal/image-generation · …/video-generation
- Follow the original company's notes above for its models (`google/…` = Google, `openai/…` = OpenAI, `x-ai/…` = xAI). For other models
  (FLUX, Recraft, Seedream, Qwen Image …) use the general rules in `image.md` — a full scene paragraph, text in quotes, no negative words.
- Video: describe motion, camera angle, lighting and composition in detail. Allowed lengths and ratios differ per model (the tool snaps to
  the nearest).

## fal.ai · Replicate (open models)
- FLUX schnell: very cheap and fast, short to medium prompts fine, **weak with text** — avoid lettering or keep it to one short word.
- Nano Banana (Replicate): same as Google above.
- Seedance / Wan / Veo videos: the `video.md` paragraph; Wan Fast makes about 5 seconds without sound.
- Music models: ElevenLabs Music and MiniMax Music take a style prompt and lyrics (MiniMax needs lyrics); Stable Audio makes instrumental
  music and sound effects only — no singing.

## Stability AI (pictures · music)
- Stable Image Core/Ultra: a clear descriptive prompt; it accepts style words well; text in pictures is limited — keep it short.
- Stable Audio: instrumental music and sound effects (no lyrics) — describe genre, instruments, tempo and mood.

## ElevenLabs Music
- Style line (genre, instruments, vocal, tempo, mood) plus lyrics with section tags; set `instrumental: true` for background music.
- Commercial use depends on the user's plan.

## Another image server (OpenAI-compatible)
- Whatever model the user's own server runs — use the general rules; if results ignore long prompts, shorten to the key sentences.
